catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.joint_position.v1 takes a flat joint_positions array and requires reached and joint_positions outputs. The pinned controller action is control_msgs/action/FollowJointTrajectory on /scaled_joint_trajectory_controller/follow_joint_trajectory: its goal is trajectory.points, an array of point objects carrying positions and time_from_start, and its terminal result is error_code and error_string. RosDriver argument targets cannot address array indices, so the flat class cannot be placed into trajectory.points; the class output also does not match the native terminal result. The extension preserves the controller's trajectory goal and terminal semantics.
catalogue_requests.summary: Send FollowJointTrajectory points through /scaled_joint_trajectory_controller/follow_joint_trajectory and report the controller's terminal error_code.

catalogue_requests.reason: cap.sensing.read.v1 is restricted to the sensor, sensor.imu and sensor.force_torque resource kinds. This device is robot.arm, and the pinned observation is a sensor_msgs/msg/JointState message on /joint_states with parallel name, position and velocity arrays. The extension carries that native message shape without relabelling the arm as a sensor.

E-stop: /controller_manager/switch_controller deactivates scaled_joint_trajectory_controller with strictness STRICT (2) and a 0.4 s timeout, confirmed by /controller_manager/list_controllers with one element named scaled_joint_trajectory_controller whose state is inactive (E4). The declared re-enable x-cap.qdeyna.activate_controller.v1 (CORE-086) activates that controller again. Deactivation aborts the goal, keeps each position command at its last value, releases the interfaces and drops the stored trajectory (joint_trajectory_controller.cpp:1055-1106). On activation this deployment holds the measured position: the command is position only and the state is position and velocity, so the command-interface read fails (cpp:498-510, 1004-1020) and the controller holds state_current_ (cpp:1027-1029, 1617-1626). The dropped trajectory is not resumed (SAFE-042). Reset releases the latch only and does not activate the controller. There is no world pause and no unpause. A switch that times out answers ok false and the e-stop stays unconfirmed with the latch held (controller_manager.cpp:1307-1331; a zero duration becomes 1 s). SwitchController.srv comments that a zero timeout is infinite; the pinned cpp substitutes 1 s. Any client of the switch service can re-activate the controller. The scaled controller requests speed_scaling_interface_name (scaled_joint_trajectory_controller.cpp:63-70). The controller manager claims every individual state interface before it calls activate and skips the controller when that claim throws (controller_manager.cpp:1653-1681; resource_manager.cpp:743-747). The on_activate search (scaled_joint_trajectory_controller.cpp:75-95) looks only at interfaces already assigned to the controller. scaling_factor_ defaults to 1.0 in the header (hpp:78); that initializer is not a deployment fallback for a missing interface. On the fake-hardware path this package serves, ur_macro.xacro:113-114 includes ur.ros2_control.xacro when use_fake_hardware is true. That description selects mock_components/GenericSystem (ur.ros2_control.xacro:44-48) and, inside the block omitted for sim_gazebo and sim_ignition, declares gpio speed_scaling with state interface speed_scaling_factor and parameter initial_speed_scaling_factor 1 (:160-166). GenericSystem exports that gpio state (generic_system.cpp:301-305) and, when the interface has no initial_value, initializes it from the component parameter initial_<interface name> (:714-726). With an empty tf_prefix, the controller yaml name speed_scaling/speed_scaling_factor is that interface. A description that omits the gpio does not reach on_activate.
